question: For the selected complete first record and fixed later physical-fault key, what is the exact total effect of changing the public red-X correction on the next complete public record, allowing final physical support to differ?
role: Small finite ideal causal-model diagnostic, not a schedule-risk, decoder-performance, threshold, or general physical-channel study
source_basis: Jing Appendix A.2/A.4 ideal red-X/projector convention

model.physical_state: Same periodic L=2 J6M vacuum orbit, private initial red-X edges [0,4,3], exact chronological ideal star projectors, no readout noise
model.first_record: The preselected J7F complete 24-site binary first public record with charge 0 at individually variable sites 1 and 2 and exact mass 1/4; it occurs before either action
model.intervention: Set the relation-free public correction to [0] or [4] after the common first record. In each future-key column, hold the same private later red-X fault [0] or [4] across the two actions; no same-final-support conditioning or post-treatment matching
model.public_private_boundary: Expose only full 24-site flux/charge/vacuum arrays, public action, and action/future-key-bound completion. Initial/future physical supports, operator masks, orbit and projector state remain private generation/scoring diagnostics, not decoder inputs
model.estimand: Within each fixed later-fault key, rational total variation of the complete next-first public laws after marginalizing each action-conditioned complete second public law, conditional on the same selected first public record. This is a finite model total action effect, not its decomposition into information versus deterministic flux
model.independent_unit_uncertainty: One exact finite orbit and one selected first record; rational Born masses and TV have no Monte Carlo interval or generalization claim

matrix.four_cells: All two actions by two fixed future keys. The J7G [0]/[0] and [4]/[4] diagonal cells must replay exactly, including their action-conditioned second/next public laws; off-diagonal cells may have different final support and next flux
matrix.law: Enumerate all positive complete second public records at the actual residual sector, all positive complete next-first public records at each resulting final sector, normalize at every prefix, marginalize the second law, and compare only actions within each common-future column
matrix.integrity: Pin before/after; exact positive first mass and public arrays; sector eligibility; J7H final support/flux; J7G diagonal replay; public/private/action/future-key binding negatives; deterministic replay; no caller mutation

competing_outcomes.flux_separated: If fixed-future action pairs have different next flux, full-public TV is exactly 1 when both complete laws normalize; report as deterministic flux separation only, without assigning it to herald-charge information or risk benefit
competing_outcomes.overlapping_public_support: If final supports differ but public flux overlaps, evaluate exact full-record TV and state that support-level difference does not itself establish public discrimination
competing_outcomes.censored: Any source, first/second/next public law, binding, replay, compute, geometry, diagonal-control or model gate fails; no contrast claim or post-hoc budget enlargement

acceptance: Seven pins pass before/after and selected first complete record has exact mass 1/4
All four action/future cells use the J7H support/flux ledger and have normalized complete second and next public laws
Both J7G diagonal cells replay their exact public laws; five negative binding controls and deterministic result replay pass
Within each common-future column compare action laws by exact rational full-public TV, explicitly distinguishing deterministic flux from charge/history information
No noisy schedule, caller, decoder-risk, threshold, stochastic, bootstrap or general-channel claim
stop_rule: Stop on any pin, geometry, eligibility, Born, diagonal replay, binding or 60-CPU-second/term/site/row cap failure. Do not select another first record, expand geometry or future keys, invoke caller, collect noisy histories, or increase caps post-data.
